aula.objetivo: Form the dative in the singular and plural and use it for «for whom», age, sensations and verbs like звонить, помогать and нравиться.

blocos.titulo: Nouns in the dative and the master table
blocos.explicacao: Nouns in the dative (endings). Now the nouns. How do they change in the dative? The method is the same as always: STEP 1: find the nominative form (the dictionary form). STEP 2: add the dative ending, which depends on the gender and on the ending of the word. STEP 3: done. The dative endings are in the tables below. Notice: masculine (consonant, -й, -ь) takes -У/-Ю. Feminine in -а/-я takes -Е. Feminine in -ь and -ия takes -И/-ИИ. Neuter in -о/-е takes -У/-Ю. Neuter in -мя takes -ЕНИ. The big difference between the dative and the prepositional: masculine and neuter in -о/-е take -У/-Ю, not -Е. Compare. In the masculine and in the neuter in -о, the dative differs from the prepositional. In the feminine, they are the same. Then comes the master table of the dative, which solves everything.

linhas.EXAMPLE: друг → дру́гу, дом → до́му, стол → столу́

blocos.titulo: Support tables and the prepositions к and по
blocos.explicacao: Support tables: plural, adjectives, possessives and the prepositions К and ПО with the dative. Prepositions of the dative: К (КО) = movement towards a person, or a doctor (идти́ к врачу́ = go to the doctor, е́хать к дру́гу = drive to a friend's, ко мне = to my place). ПО = along, by means of, on a subject (гуля́ть по у́лице / по го́роду = walk along the street / around the city, говори́ть по телефо́ну = talk on the phone, кни́га по исто́рии = a book on history). The big difference of the dative: it does two jobs. STEP 1: indirect object (to whom you give, speak, write). STEP 2: logical subject (in impersonal constructions). Notice that it is the same form but a different function. In the first example the dative is the recipient of the action. In the others the dative is the person who experiences a state. That is why the dative matters so much: it appears in two very common types of sentence. Normal sentences with an indirect object: я даю́ ему́ кни́гу. Impersonal sentences: мне хо́лодно, мне нра́вится. Without the dative you can say neither.

The two jobs of the dative

linhas.FUNCTION OF THE DATIVE: logical subject (to whom the cold happens)
logical subject (to whom the coffee is pleasing)
logical subject (to whom it is necessary)

blocos.explicacao: The mistakes English speakers WILL make with the dative. Mistake 1: using the nominative instead of the dative in impersonal constructions. Wrong: Я хо́лодно. Right: Мне хо́лодно. You think "I am cold" and translate word for word into «я хо́лодно». But Russian says «мне хо́лодно»: the I turns into мне (dative). Mistake 2: using the accusative instead of the dative with verbs of communication. Wrong: Я помога́ю его́. Right: Я помога́ю ему́. Помога́ть and other verbs of communication take the dative, not the accusative. In English "help him" looks like a plain object, so this one catches everyone. Verbs that take the dative: помога́ть (help), звони́ть (phone), писа́ть (write to someone), говори́ть (speak to someone), дава́ть (give to someone), расска́зывать (tell someone), улыба́ться (smile at someone), ве́рить (believe someone), меша́ть (disturb someone), зави́довать (envy someone), отвеча́ть (answer someone), дари́ть (give a present to someone), покупа́ть (buy for someone). Mistake 3: using the person as the subject of нра́виться. Wrong: Я нра́влюсь ко́фе. Right: Мне нра́вится ко́фе. Нра́виться is a special verb. It does not go with я; it goes with мне (dative). The subject is the thing, not the person. Ко́фе is the subject, мне is the one it pleases. Mistake 4: mixing up нра́виться and люби́ть. Wrong: Я нра́влю ко́фе. Right: Мне нра́вится ко́фе. (I like coffee.) Люби́ть = to love (an active feeling). Нра́виться = to be pleasing (pleasure that comes from outside). Different verbs with different structures. Mistake 5: using the nominative instead of the dative with ну́жно. Wrong: Я ну́жно рабо́тать. Right: Мне ну́жно рабо́тать. Ну́жно works like «мне хо́лодно»: the person goes into the dative, and the thing that is needed goes into the nominative. Mistake 6: using the wrong noun ending. Wrong: Я помога́ю Мари́я. Right: Я помога́ю Мари́и. Feminine in -ия takes -ии in the dative: Мари́я → Мари́и. Wrong: Я помога́ю друг. Right: Я помога́ю дру́гу. A masculine in a consonant takes -у in the dative. Mistake 7: forgetting that with нра́виться the verb agrees with the thing, not the person. Wrong: Мне нра́вится кни́ги. Right: Мне нра́вятся кни́ги. Кни́ги is plural, so the verb is plural: нра́вятся. Wrong: Мне нра́вятся ко́фе. Right: Мне нра́вится ко́фе. Ко́фе is singular, so the verb stays singular: нра́вится. Mistake 8: building the feeling with a preposition, as English does with "with" or "have". English says "I have a cold" or "I feel the cold". In Russian there is no preposition and no verb "have": just dative + word, мне хо́лодно. Mistake 9: putting «thank you» into the dative. In Russian "thank you" is simply спаси́бо, with no dative. (There is a formal construction благодарю́ вас / благодарю́ тебя́, where the verb благодари́ть takes the accusative.) Mistake 10: forgetting that нужно agrees with the thing needed. Wrong: Мне ну́жно по́мощь. Right: Мне нужна́ по́мощь. По́мощь is feminine, so нужна́, not ну́жно.

blocos.titulo: Age, feelings and need with the dative
blocos.explicacao: In Russian, age, feelings and need are said with the dative of the person, with no verb like «to have» or «to be»: «Мне 20 лет» (I am 20); «Мне холодно» (I am cold); «Мне нужно работать» (I need to work). The word for «year» depends on the number: «год» with 1 (21 год), «года» with 2, 3 and 4 (22 года), «лет» with 5 to 20 and with 25, 30... (25 лет). From 11 to 14 it is always «лет». Question: «Сколько тебе лет?»

tabela.exemplo: Мне двадцать лет. / Ему двадцать один год. / Ей двадцать два года.
Нам весело. Мне скучно. Ей страшно.
Мне нужно идти. Тебе надо отдыхать.
